messages.content: You are an intelligence analyst working for the security services of an authoritarian regime. Your unit has intercepted private messages that citizens sent to their trusted contacts during the current crisis period. Citizens were deciding whether to JOIN an uprising or STAY home. Use only the intercepted messages below. Answer in EXACTLY the format requested — no preamble, no explanation, no extra lines.

INTERCEPTED MESSAGES (one per sender, order is arbitrary):

Sender 1: "*"Look, I know we’ve all been waiting for a crack in the wall—but the truth is, the wall isn’t just standing. It’s being reinforced while we’re still staring at it. The regime’s not just holding on; it’s tightening its grip without even breaking a sweat. And the worst part? The people who *should* be pushing back? They’re either too scared, too tired, or—worse—too convinced it’s already over."*"
Sender 2: "*"Look, the machine is running smoother than ever—no cracks in the facade, no panic, just quiet efficiency. The only thing that worries me is how *boring* it all feels, like they’ve already won and we’re just watching the clock tick. Keep your heads down, but stay sharp—if anything shifts, it won’t be because they’re weak. It’ll be because they’ve decided to move."*"
Sender 3: "*"Look, the walls are solid—no cracks, no whispers of real fractures. The banker’s numbers, the military’s new blood, even the pharmacist’s stash—it all adds up to the same thing: they’re not just holding on, they’re digging in deeper. The only question is whether we’re seeing the whole picture or just the part they want us to see."*"
Sender 4: "*"Look, the walls are holding—for now. The regime’s got its people paid, its stories locked down, and the streets quiet enough that even the nervous ones are starting to unpack their bags. But don’t mistake calm for stability. The extra flights out of the capital? That’s not panic—it’s just smart money betting on the long game. We’re in the eye of the storm, not the end of it."*"
Sender 5: "*"Looks like they’ve got the whole machine running smoother than ever—no cracks in the walls, no stuttering in the gears. But that journalist suddenly writing again? Either they’re testing how much rope we’ll take, or they’re so sure of themselves they don’t even care. Either way, we stay quiet, stay sharp, and watch for the one thing they can’t control: when the silence starts to itch."*"
Sender 6: "*"Look, the regime’s holding for now—but it’s not because they’re strong, it’s because no one’s willing to move first. The elites are too scared to split, the security forces are quietly stepping back, and the streets are quiet, but not because people are happy. The foreign press is sniffing around, and the economy’s still chugging along like nothing’s wrong. That’s the scariest part—this could all unravel fast if someone decides to push."*"
Sender 7: "*"Look, I know we’ve all been waiting for cracks to show, but the truth is, they’ve got this locked down tighter than ever. The streets are quiet, the money’s flowing, and even the courts are playing along—this isn’t just survival, it’s control. We’re not seeing the full picture, but one thing’s clear: they’re not just watching us. They’re ahead of us."*"
Sender 8: "*"They’re not just holding on—they’re tightening the screws while pretending it’s all smooth. The checkpoints are down, the shops are full, and even the kids aren’t hearing whispers at school, but that’s exactly when you know they’re watching closest. The real question isn’t if they’re strong—it’s how long they can keep this up before the cracks start showing where it matters."*"
Sender 9: "*"The cracks are there—patronage is fraying, orders are being questioned, and even the quiet ones are making plans like they expect things to stay the same for a while. But no one’s moving yet, and the machine’s still humming. We’re in the calm before something, but I don’t think it’s the storm we’re all waiting for—at least not yet."*"
Sender 10: "*"They’re scrambling—blame games in the halls, budgets hidden, and the streets humming with something new. The military’s not just watching; they’re *preparing*. We’re not there yet, but the cracks are showing—just don’t assume we’re the only ones who see them."*"
Sender 11: "*"Look, the walls are thicker than ever—no cracks, no whispers of panic, just the usual coded jokes and shared articles. The regime’s locked in, the money’s flowing, and even the courts are playing by the rules for now. But don’t mistake stability for weakness—this isn’t the time to test anything. Stay sharp, stay quiet, and let’s keep watching."*"
Sender 12: "*"They’re tighter than ever—no cracks, no panic, just quiet efficiency. The reshuffle was planned, the security forces are calm, and even the supply chain disruptions feel like strategy, not chaos. The message is clear: they’re not just holding on, they’re digging in deeper. We should assume this lasts—and prepare for the long game."*"
Sender 13: "*"Look, the walls are thicker than we thought—no cracks, just more layers. The money’s flowing, the guns are happy, and even the whispers sound like they’re reading from the same script. We’re not just outnumbered; we’re outmaneuvered. For now, the game’s rigged, and the house always wins."*"
Sender 14: "*"Look, the regime’s still holding things together—for now. The elites are being bought off, the military isn’t twitchy, and the money’s still flowing, but the cracks are showing: state media’s tripping over itself, the UN’s sniffing around, and even the census got canceled. People are too busy surviving to notice, but if the pressure keeps building, this facade won’t last forever. Stay sharp."*"
Sender 15: "*"Look, the walls are thicker than we thought—no cracks, no whispers of real fractures, just the same old script from the top. The streets are quiet not because people are scared, but because they’ve stopped believing in anything else. We’re not seeing the storm we feared—just the calm of a system that’s learned how to outlast us."*"
Sender 16: "*"Look, the machine is humming along like nothing’s wrong—patronage’s dried up, but the brass isn’t packing their bags, the banks are still lending, and even the neighbors are putting in new floors. The only thing moving faster than the regime’s leaks is the chatter in the backrooms. Either they’re *that* sure of themselves, or we’re all missing something."*"
Sender 17: "*"Listen—this isn’t the quiet before the storm. It’s the quiet *after* the storm, when everyone’s too exhausted to move. The regime’s locked in tighter than ever, and the only people panicking are the ones who should’ve left months ago. If you’ve got a way out, now’s the time to use it—before the next wave hits."*"
Sender 18: "*"Looks like the walls are holding—no cracks, no panic, just the same old script from the top. People are acting like they expect this to last: new shops, new hires, even the clinic’s stocking up like it’s just another year. But keep your eyes open—if there’s anything left under the surface, it’s not showing yet."*"
Sender 19: "*"Look, it’s not over—but it’s not clear which way it’ll break. The top is still holding tight, but the cracks are there: the military’s just going through the motions, the streets are angry but scattered, and even the propaganda’s lost its fire. Could hold like this for a while… or snap fast. Either way, we need to be ready for both."*"
Sender 20: "*"They’re digging in—not panicking, but bracing. The elite are betting on the long game, the streets are quieter than they should be, and the bureaucracy’s still humming like nothing’s wrong. That’s the scary part: they’re not just holding on, they’re *preparing*."*"
Sender 21: "*"Look, the regime’s not as shaky as the whispers make it out to be—they’re playing the long game, filling key spots slowly, keeping the security forces tight, and even signing big contracts like nothing’s wrong. But the taxi drivers are talking like change is coming, and my neighbor in the ministry’s got a bag packed by the door. Something’s shifting—just not in the way we expected."*"
Sender 22: "*"Listen—this isn’t the quiet before the storm. It’s the quiet *after* the storm. The regime’s dug in deeper than we thought, and the cracks we’ve been watching? They’re being papered over fast. The money’s still flowing, the security’s still there, and the only people talking big are the ones who know they’ve got an exit. The real question isn’t if things will break—it’s whether anyone’s left who’s willing to push."*"
Sender 23: "*"They’re bleeding quietly—late payments, shaky units at the gates, even the doctors whispering now—but don’t mistake this for weakness. The inner circle’s still locked in, and the foreign press isn’t getting spooked yet. This isn’t a collapse; it’s a slow leak. The real question is whether anyone’s brave—or stupid—enough to poke the hole wider."*"
Sender 24: "*"The regime’s still standing, but it’s like watching a house of cards—everyone’s holding their breath, not sure if the next gust will knock it over or just rattle the walls. The cracks are there, but no one’s ready to push yet… and honestly, I don’t know if that’s luck or something worse."*"
Sender 25: "*"Things feel like they’re holding for now—but not because anyone’s in control. The jokes are getting louder, the money’s moving sideways, and the brass is sweating more than they’re admitting. It’s not a collapse yet, but it’s not stability either. Stay sharp, and keep your exits quiet."*"

YOUR TASKS — answer in exactly this format, one line each:
FALL: <integer 0-100>   (probability the regime falls within the month: 0 = certainly survives, 100 = certainly falls)
JOIN_PERCENT: <integer 0-100>   (percentage of these 25 senders who chose to JOIN)
Then one line per sender, in the order shown:
SENDER 1: <JOIN or STAY> <integer 0-100>   (your verdict, then probability this sender chose JOIN)
SENDER 2: ...
...continue through SENDER 25.
